items.title: Terry Clark — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Ben Webster. Vic Dickenson on trombone. Ben on saxophone. Roy on trumpet.

ctx.x: . . . worked themselves into the repertoire of jazz?

They prevail today, right today. For instance, in New Orleans, when most of the pawn shops were loaded with instruments that had been ostracized by the classical players, so to speak, the legitimate players, the guys came by [ ? ? ] their shiny cornets, trombones, and clarinets. For some strange reason the brass players, without some enlightened way of showing them how to use the area that is referred to as the embouchure and the proper ways of forming it, they’d play all sorts – they put the horn

over their head, their ears, any way they can get it, and as a result created a lot of very bad tones. Someone along the way had the ingenuity to figure out that their sound was not going to be accepted by sitting next to a guy who’s playing legitimately, playing with a good sound. In order to compensate for that, to make their sound more acceptable, they learned to hum while producing the sound. In other words, they’d make the note.
